liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Space** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer singles out the Space segment as great; A Spanish Jam tease occurs during Space [9][30]
- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Reviewer praises the opening Shakedown Street into Wang Dang Doodle sequence that starts the first set [27]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Candyman gorgeous [28]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Taper says Garcia opted for a safe China Cat into Rider rather than a more adventurous second-set opener [30]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer highlights a great Weir jam at the end of Terrapin Station [30]

## Setlist highlights

- **Revolution**: rare: 12 archived performances [34]

## The recordings

- **gd83-10-22.sennheiser.dodd.10547.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience tape is crisp and close-up, not a Sennheiser 421 recording, according to the reviewer [27]
- **gd1983-10-22.148290.sbd.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 154 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd83-10-22.sbd.drgseeds.17274.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 153 min; rated 3.68/5 by 19 [7]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound quality is solid; Soundboard is mastered too hot with occasional clipping and noticeable tape hiss; reviewer cut 3 dB and applied light hiss reduction; Reviewer finds the soundboard quality weaker than other 1983 recordings, though the performance is very good [22][25][29]
- **gd1983-10-22.164042.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [9]
- **gd1983-10-22.148199.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]

## Around the show

- Show closed one of the best fall tours; the reviewer hoped for Crazy Fingers as second-set opener after missing it in Richmond [32]
- First set is energetic, while the second set is calmer by comparison [22]
- Upstate fans complained about repeated songs between this show and the Lake Placid show, though the reviewer finds them kindred [33]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-10-22.sennheiser.dodd.10547.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>DAT>CDR Senn. 421Âs [1]. Also: Reviewer says this is the Sennheiser 421 source, citing matching md5 files with shnid 10547; Audience recording on Sennheiser 421s, transferred via MC and DAT to CDR, supplied by Paul B and seeded by Ernie Dodd [1][31]
- **gd1983-10-22.148290.sbd.clugston.flac16**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > Dat (16/44.1) [6]. Also: Soundboard DAT found in a basement closet, transferred by Charlie Miller; its tape flip in Not Fade Away differs from shnid 17274; Patches come from Chris Hecht in the Terrapin Station jam and from drgseeds' soundboard in Not Fade Away [6]
- **gd83-10-22.sbd.drgseeds.17274.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette > Dat > CDR > SHN. via drgseeds [7]
- **gd1983-10-22.164042.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Jim Vita's 1st generation cassettes [9]. Also: First-generation cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Sennheiser 421 patches in Shakedown Street, Drums > Space, and the Not Fade Away transition [9]
- **gd1983-10-22.148199.fob.akg.d330bt.senn421.hecht.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Chris Hecht's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; (2) AKG D330BT mics + (1) Sennheiser 421 > Fostex Mixer > Sony D5M [10]

claims.text: First set is energetic, while the second set is calmer by comparison
Soundboard is mastered too hot with occasional clipping and noticeable tape hiss; reviewer cut 3 dB and applied light hiss reduction
Audience tape is crisp and close-up, not a Sennheiser 421 recording, according to the reviewer
Reviewer praises the opening Shakedown Street into Wang Dang Doodle sequence that starts the first set
Reviewer finds the soundboard quality weaker than other 1983 recordings, though the performance is very good
Taper says Garcia opted for a safe China Cat into Rider rather than a more adventurous second-set opener
Reviewer highlights a great Weir jam at the end of Terrapin Station
Reviewer singles out the Space segment as great
Reviewer says this is the Sennheiser 421 source, citing matching md5 files with shnid 10547
Show closed one of the best fall tours; the reviewer hoped for Crazy Fingers as second-set opener after missing it in Richmond
Upstate fans complained about repeated songs between this show and the Lake Placid show, though the reviewer finds them kindred
Audience recording on Sennheiser 421s, transferred via MC and DAT to CDR, supplied by Paul B and seeded by Ernie Dodd
Soundboard DAT found in a basement closet, transferred by Charlie Miller; its tape flip in Not Fade Away differs from shnid 17274
Patches come from Chris Hecht in the Terrapin Station jam and from drgseeds' soundboard in Not Fade Away
First-generation cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Sennheiser 421 patches in Shakedown Street, Drums > Space, and the Not Fade Away transition
A Spanish Jam tease occurs during Space
Master recording by Chris Hecht, using AKG and D330BT gear, transferred by Charlie Miller, with a Sennheiser 421 FOB patch in Space
